# Feature: Unified Run-Event Stream

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-063
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_ui.md`

Every Yantra run (terminal, app worker or daemon) writes one ordered, sequence-numbered record of
what happened while it ran: `<runDir>/run-events.jsonl`. Today that history is split across
places. Workflow lifecycle events go to `events.jsonl`. Agent progress exists only as terminal
lines, because `AgentProgressEvent` is an `@yantra/agent` type that is never persisted.
Deterministic `ask`/`research` show nothing between the goal echo and the result. A consent wait
leaves no surface-neutral record.

This feature defines one `RunEvent` union in `@yantra/protocol` and a single-writer log with a
persist-before-publish rule, defined flush points and recovery of a partial tail. The CLI's
terminal and `--json` renderers become consumers of that union, and their output stays
byte-identical. The app (FEAT-064 sockets, FEAT-067 cockpit) and any future connector then read
one contract, with no screen-scraping of terminal text. The feature also adds the `owner_lost`
and `user_app` enum values that ownership (FEAT-064) and app consent (FEAT-068) depend on, with
compatibility fixtures in both directions.

**What the user sees.** No CLI output changes. A new artifact, `run-events.jsonl`, appears in every
new run directory and is listed in `report.md`'s Audit Trail.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

> `.spec-lite/data_model.md` does not exist. The model below is designed here from plan_ui §6
> (Protocol additions; Artifacts and state), §8 (Event log contract), §12 FEAT-063 and §15 (the
> open question on phase-event shapes, resolved here). Storage is filesystem JSONL, not a
> database. All schemas are Zod with `.describe()` on every field (memory → Documentation), so
> `docs/protocol-spec.md` and the emitted JSON Schema derive from them.

### Entities & Attributes

- **RunEventRecord** (one line of `run-events.jsonl`; also the payload of the FEAT-064 socket
  `event` message):
  - `schema_version` (literal `'1'`, `RUN_EVENTS_SCHEMA_VERSION`). Envelope version. A reader
    rejects an unknown major and reads any line whose version it knows. NOT NULL.
  - `seq` (integer ≥ 1). Gap-free, strictly increasing within one file. Assigned by the writer at
    append time and never by the producer. NOT NULL.
  - `run_id` (string, min 1). The owning run. NOT NULL.
  - `event` (`RunEvent`). NOT NULL.

- **RunEvent** (discriminated union on `kind`; every variant has `at`, an ISO-8601 UTC datetime
  of emission):
  - **Every existing `TaskEvent` variant**, spread in unchanged (`task_queued` …
    `discovery_session_completed`, with `task_id`). `events.jsonl` keeps receiving exactly what it
    receives today; `run-events.jsonl` receives a mirror.
  - **Agent progress variants** promoted from `@yantra/agent`. Each variant's fields are defined
    **once** as a shared shape, which builds two unions: `AgentProgressEvent` (discriminator
    `type`, the existing connector type, re-exported from `@yantra/agent`) and the matching
    `RunEvent` variants (discriminator `kind`). Field names stay exactly as today, including
    camelCase `durationMs`, so `do --json` stays byte-identical (see Design notes).
    - `recovery` — `rung` (`steer|freeze|stop`), `trigger` (`stalled|turn-timeout`), `move`
      (`fill-remaining|list-fields|capture|publish|null`), `summary`.
    - `progress` — `items` (`LiveItem[]`: `id`, `kind` `fill|artifact|effects|deliverable`,
      `label`, `state` `pending|advancing|met`, `done` int|null, `total` int|null), `summary`.
    - `assistant_text` — `text`.
    - `tool_started` — `tool`, `summary`.
    - `tool_finished` — `tool`, `summary`, `status` (`ok|error|denied|aborted`), `durationMs`
      (int|null).
    - `contract_declared` — `revision` (int ≥ 1), `summary`.
    - `capability_gap` — `item`, `reason` (`DeliverableCaptureReason`), `summary`.
  - **New variants:**
    - `goal_echo` — `display` (string ≤ 260; the exact echo line without its newline, e.g.
      `goal: "…"` or `goal: [not shown: …]`), `received_chars` (int ≥ 0), `truncated` (bool).
      The text is already redacted by `redactRunInput` and control-stripped.
    - `run_warning` — `source` (`command|agent`), `text` (string ≤ 1000, control-stripped). It is
      the counterpart of every `warning: …` advisory line a run prints today (see §2 Counterpart
      table). _Plan addition, required by the acceptance item "every live event has a
      counterpart"._
    - `receipt_written` — `path` (literal `execution-receipt.json`), `sha256` (64 lowercase hex).
    - `budget_snapshot` — `dimensions` (array of at most 16 items, each with `name` (snake_case
      token ≤ 48), `used` (number ≥ 0), `limit` (number ≥ 0 | null) and `unit`
      (`ms|count|bytes|pixels`)). One generic shape serves the agent `BudgetTracker` and the
      research `BudgetTracker`.
    - `artifact_saved` — `path` (run-relative POSIX path ≤ 300 with no `..` segment and no
      leading `/`), `artifact_kind` (`brief|report|templated_report|screenshot|output|result|other`),
      `media_type` (string ≤ 100), `bytes` (int ≥ 0 | null).
    - `intervention_raised` — `intervention_id` (the `confirmation_id`), `intervention_kind`
      (`confirmation`; FEAT-068 extends the enum additively), `request` (`ConfirmationRequest`),
      `deadline_at` (datetime | null; absolute, D5).
    - `intervention_resolved` — `intervention_id`, `decision` (`granted|denied|timed_out`),
      `decided_by` (`ConfirmationDecidedBy`), `decided_at` (datetime).
    - `run_outcome` — `run_id`, `task_outcome` (`TaskOutcome`), `termination_reason`
      (`TerminationReason` | null), `stop_detail` (snake_case token ≤ 64 | null; command-specific
      detail such as research's `max_hops` or `coverage_met`), `exit_code` (int), `failure_class`
      (`FailureClass` | null). **Exactly one per run**, and it is the run's last event.
    - **Deterministic `ask`/`research` phase events** (resolves plan §15; bounded and sanitized
      like agent progress):
      - `search_completed` — `hop_index` (int ≥ 1 | null; null for `ask`), `provider` (token
        ≤ 48), `query` (string ≤ 200, passed through `redactRunInput` and control-stripped),
        `result_count` (int ≥ 0), `cached` (bool).
      - `source_fetched` — `hop_index` (int | null), `source_index` (int ≥ 1), `url` (string ≤ 300:
        origin plus path only; userinfo, query and fragment are dropped, and a credential-shaped
        path becomes `<origin>/[redacted]`), `status` (`ok|failed|blocked|skipped`),
        `failure_class` (token ≤ 48 | null), `duration_ms` (int ≥ 0 | null).
      - `extract_completed` — `hop_index` (int | null), `extracted` (int ≥ 0), `failed` (int ≥ 0).
      - `synthesize_started` — `strategy` (`deterministic|llm`), `sources_in` (int ≥ 0).
        Completion is the existing `synthesis_completed` `TaskEvent`.
    - `event_omitted` — `original_kind` (string ≤ 64), `bytes` (int). The writer substitutes it
      for any event whose serialized line would exceed `MAX_RUN_EVENT_LINE_BYTES` (256 KiB),
      which keeps every record well under the 1 MiB socket message cap (§6). _Plan addition._

- **Protocol enum changes** (D7, §6 Protocol additions):
  - `TerminationReason` gains `owner_lost`.
  - `ConfirmationDecidedBy` gains `user_app`.
  - `TaskEvent.confirmation_resolved.decided_by` stops being an inline enum and references
    `ConfirmationDecidedBy`, so both stay in step. There is still no agent variant.

- **RunEventDelivery** (in-process only; never persisted). The value that in-process subscribers
  receive:
  - `seq` (number | null): null only for a pre-open or degraded delivery.
  - `committed` (bool): true iff the line was appended before delivery.
  - `event` (`RunEvent`).

- **RunEventReadItem** (reader output):
  - `{status: 'event', record}`;
  - `{status: 'unknown_kind', seq, kind, raw}`: a well-formed envelope from a newer writer. It
    feeds the app's `EventInspector` (D17) and is never an error.
  - `{status: 'invalid', line, reason}`: a complete line that is not a valid envelope. It is
    skipped and reported.

  A trailing partial line (no terminating `\n`) is never an item. The reader ignores it.

### Relationships

- Run directory 1:1 `run-events.jsonl` (created by the run's single writer).
- `run-events.jsonl` 1:N `RunEventRecord`, ordered by `seq`.
- `RunEventRecord` (TaskEvent variants) 1:1 mirror of the same `events.jsonl` line (same object,
  written by both sinks).
- `intervention_raised.intervention_id` = `ConfirmationRequest.confirmation_id` =
  `confirmations.jsonl` request id; `intervention_resolved.intervention_id` joins to it.
- `artifact_saved.path` resolves under the run directory (FEAT-066 serves only allowlisted kinds).
- `receipt_written.path` → `execution-receipt.json` (FEAT-072).

### Indexes & Constraints

- **Single writer per file.** Only the run's owning process appends. FEAT-064's lease enforces
  ownership and its reconciler appends only after its claim. _STUB: until FEAT-064 lands, ownership
  is by construction, because only the process that created the run directory opens the log._
- `seq` is strictly increasing by 1 from the last valid line. On open, the writer truncates a
  trailing partial line, then continues from the last valid `seq`.
- Exactly one `run_outcome` per run, written last. A second `run_outcome` emit is rejected with
  `RunEventLogError` code `RUN_OUTCOME_DUPLICATE`.
- **Fsync points** (`RunEventLog` flush policy):
  - immediately after any **intervention change** (`intervention_raised`, `intervention_resolved`,
    `confirmation_requested`, `confirmation_resolved`, `human_handoff_requested`);
  - immediately after any **terminal** event (`run_outcome`, `task_completed`, `task_failed`);
  - otherwise once 50 events have been appended since the last sync, or 1 second after the first
    unsynced append, whichever comes first (thresholds are constants pending §15 confirmation);
  - on `close()`.
- Line cap `MAX_RUN_EVENT_LINE_BYTES` = 262,144 (UTF-8 bytes, including the newline).
- **Never in the log:** secret values, resolved `{{user:…}}` placeholder values, raw page text,
  full URLs with query or userinfo, environment values, tokens, frames.

### Counterpart table (acceptance: "every live event a CLI run shows today has a counterpart")

| Live output today (source)                                                                                                     | Counterpart `RunEvent`                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `goal: "…"` echo, stderr (`render/goal-echo.ts`, `ask`/`research`/`do`)                                                        | `goal_echo`                                                     |
| `warning: …` advisories (`CLIConnectorIO.emitAgentWarning`; `run`/`ask`/`research` model-unavailable and template-guard lines) | `run_warning`                                                   |
| `[tool] summary` / `[tool] status — summary (Nms)` (`emitAgentEvent`)                                                          | `tool_started` / `tool_finished`                                |
| assistant text stream                                                                                                          | `assistant_text`                                                |
| `understood: …` / `understood (revised): …`                                                                                    | `contract_declared`                                             |
| `progress: …`, `recovery: …`                                                                                                   | `progress`, `recovery`                                          |
| capability-gap disclosure line                                                                                                 | `capability_gap`                                                |
| `--json` `agent_progress` NDJSON lines                                                                                         | the agent variants above                                        |
| terminal consent card and `[y/N]` prompt (`InteractiveConfirmationGateway`, `CLIConnectorIO.requestConfirmation`)              | `intervention_raised` / `intervention_resolved`                 |
| outcome first line, `Screenshot:` lines, `Run: <id>`, `Handoff:`/`Failed:`/`Aborted:` lines, `--json` `agent_outcome`          | `run_outcome` (+ `artifact_saved` per screenshot or Brief file) |
| `✓/✗/⤺ Run <id>: <outcome>` / `Resume <id>: …` (`run`, `resume`)                                                               | `run_outcome`                                                   |
| Brief / templated report rendered at the end (`renderResult`)                                                                  | `artifact_saved` (+ `synthesis_completed` where applicable)     |

Result **documents** (the rendered Brief, `--json` result envelopes) remain the command's result
output, rendered by the existing result path. FEAT-072 turns that path into a result transport.
The live **events** listed above are the ones rendered from the union.

### Design notes

- **Persist before publish, and its one pre-open exception** (see DEVIATION below). Once the log
  is open, every event is appended (write completed) before any subscriber sees it. Committed
  subscribers, the default kind (sockets, tests, future app relays), only ever see appended
  events. Only a subscriber that opts in with `includeUncommitted: true` (the owning process's
  terminal or JSON renderer) receives events emitted **before the log is open**: the goal echo and
  pre-run warnings, written before the run directory exists. Those events are then committed as
  the first lines of the log, with `seq` from 1, and their original `at`. They are not delivered
  to the opted-in renderer a second time.
- **Synchronous append.** `emit()` stays synchronous for every existing producer (executor
  `publish`, connector callbacks). The writer appends with `fs.writeSync` on a descriptor opened
  for append, then publishes, then calls `fdatasync` only at fsync points. Lines are small and
  events are bounded, so the cost is a few microseconds per event.
- **Degraded mode.** If an append throws (for example `ENOSPC` or `EACCES`), the stream logs one
  structured `error` (`run_events_degraded`, error code only), stops writing and stops delivering
  to committed subscribers. It keeps delivering to `includeUncommitted` subscribers with
  `seq: null`, so the terminal behaves exactly as today and a disk fault never aborts the user's
  run. FEAT-064 decides how a degraded log is surfaced to the app.
- **`durationMs` stays camelCase** in the agent variants. The `--json` `agent_progress` lines
  print `event` verbatim today; renaming the field would change bytes that scripts parse. The
  `toAgentProgressEvent` / `toRunEvent` mappers only rename `type` ↔ `kind` and preserve key
  order, which the byte-identical golden test pins.

> **DEVIATION** (clarification of plan §8 "Persist before publish"): Plan says that an event is
> appended before it reaches renderers or sockets. The goal echo and pre-run warnings are printed
> today before the run directory exists, and before validation that can end the command with no
> run at all. Strict persist-first would delay the echo, or lose it, and break the "golden output
> unchanged" acceptance. This spec lets **only the owning process's own renderer**
> (`includeUncommitted`) see those pre-open events, then commits them first when the log opens.
> No socket, host or committed subscriber can exist before the log opens, so the D11/D17 replay
> guarantees are unaffected. Awaiting confirmation.

## 4. Dependencies

- **None blocking.** Plan §8 Sequencing: FEAT-063 can start alongside FEAT-072.
- **FEAT-072 (parallel; coordination, not a blocker).** FEAT-072 rewrites command handlers to take
  output and completion as explicit dependencies, and adds `execution-receipt.json`.
  - TASK-010 edits the same handlers (`ask`, `research`, `do`, `run`, `resume`) only to create the
    stream and pass it down. Whichever feature lands second rebases onto the other. If FEAT-072
    has landed, the stream is created from the adapter-supplied output dependency instead of
    inside the handler.
  - TASK-012 wires `receipt_written` to FEAT-072's receipt writer.
    _STUB: if the receipt writer does not exist yet, TASK-012 ships the variant and the
    `emitReceiptWritten` helper with a test, and FEAT-072 calls it._
- **Consumed later by:**
  - FEAT-064: socket replay from `readRunEvents`, the `run_outcome`/`owner_lost` reconciler
    append, and lease-enforced single writer;
  - FEAT-067: cockpit instruments keyed by `RunEvent.kind`;
  - FEAT-068: `Intervention` extends `intervention_kind` additively and adds `user_app` stamping;
  - FEAT-070: parity over `RUN_EVENT_KINDS`.

### TASK-005: Implement the single-writer `RunEventLog` and reader, with tail recovery and fsync points

- [ ] **Implementation**: - `packages/core/src/run-events/log.ts`: - `RunEventLog.open({runDir, runId, clock, sync?, logger})` scans the existing
      `run-events.jsonl` with `scanRunEventsTail`. If the file ends in a partial line, it
      truncates to the last `\n`. It sets `nextSeq` = last valid `seq` + 1 (or 1), then opens
      the file with flag `'a'`. - `append(event): number` serializes the record. Over `MAX_RUN_EVENT_LINE_BYTES` it
      substitutes `event_omitted`. It writes with `fs.writeSync` and returns `seq`. - fsync (`fs.fdatasyncSync`, injectable as `sync`) runs at the §2 fsync points. The
      interval sync uses an unref'd timer driven by the injected clock or scheduler. - A second `run_outcome` throws `RunEventLogError('RUN_OUTCOME_DUPLICATE')`. - `close()` is idempotent, syncs, then closes. An `append` after close throws
      `RunEventLogError('RUN_EVENT_LOG_CLOSED')`; the stream decides how to handle it. - `reader.ts`: - `readRunEvents(path, {fromSeq})` streams lines with `readline` (safe for 50,000
      events), ignores a trailing partial line, and yields `RunEventReadItem`s with
      `seq >= fromSeq`; - `scanRunEventsTail(path)` returns `{lastSeq, validBytes, partialTail}`. - Export `RUN_EVENTS_FILENAME`.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**: `packages/core/tests/run-events/log.spec.ts` and `reader.spec.ts`: - a fresh file starts at seq 1 and is gap-free over 1,000 appends; - **truncated tail**: a file ending mid-line is truncated on open, and the next append
      continues at `lastSeq + 1`; the reader ignores the partial line without reopening; - a complete-but-malformed middle line is `invalid` and skipped, and `seq` continues from
      the maximum valid `seq`; - **fsync points** on a stepped clock with a counting `sync` stub: an intervention kind and
      a terminal kind sync immediately; 49 ordinary events do not sync and the 50th does; one
      event syncs after 1 second; `close()` syncs; - an oversize event becomes `event_omitted` with the original kind and byte count; - a duplicate `run_outcome` throws; - append after close throws the typed error; - `readRunEvents({fromSeq: 500})` yields from 500.

### TASK-006: Implement `RunEventStream` with persist-before-publish, the pre-open buffer and degraded mode

- [ ] **Implementation**: Create `packages/core/src/run-events/stream.ts`. - **Before open.** `RunEventStream` starts **pre-open**. `emit(event)` buffers the event
      (at most 64 events; overflow drops the oldest and counts the drops) and delivers it
      immediately only to subscribers registered with `{includeUncommitted: true}`, with
      `committed: false, seq: null`. - **Opening.** `open({runDir, runId, logger, clock})` opens the `RunEventLog` and appends
      the buffered events in order, keeping their `at`. It delivers them to committed
      subscribers only; `includeUncommitted` subscribers already saw them. - **After open.** `emit` appends first, then delivers to every subscriber with
      `committed: true` and the assigned `seq`. - **Subscribers.** `subscribe(listener, opts)` returns an idempotent disposer. A listener
      that throws is isolated: logged once per listener at `warn`, without stopping delivery to
      others or the run. - **Degraded mode.** An append failure sets `degraded`, logs one `error` `run_events_degraded`
      `{code}`, and from then on delivers only to `includeUncommitted` subscribers with
      `seq: null`. - **Closing.** `close()` closes the log. A later emit is dropped, with one `warn`
      `run_events_after_close` `{kind}` per kind. - **`MirroringEventBus`.** Create `mirroring-event-bus.ts`: an `EventBus` decorator whose
      `publish(e)` calls the inner `JsonlEventBus.publish(e)` (so `events.jsonl` is unchanged)
      and `stream.emit(e)`, with `flush` and `close` delegated. Add the factory
      `openTaskEventBus(runDir, stream)`.
- [ ] **Unit Tests**: `packages/core/tests/run-events/stream.spec.ts`: - a committed subscriber never receives an event before its line exists on disk (the
      listener reads the file synchronously and finds the line); - pre-open events reach `includeUncommitted` subscribers immediately, are committed as seq
      1..n on open, and are **not** re-delivered to them; - a committed subscriber receives pre-open events only after open; - pre-open overflow keeps the newest 64; - a throwing listener does not affect others; - degraded mode, with an injected failing writer, keeps local delivery and stops committed
      delivery, logging once; - an emit after close is dropped and logged once; - `MirroringEventBus` writes the identical object to `events.jsonl` and to
      `run-events.jsonl`, and `events.jsonl` bytes equal what `JsonlEventBus` alone writes for
      the same sequence.
- [ ] **Documentation Update**: Invoke **Document** update mode for architecture (run event flow: producers → stream → log → subscribers).
- **Verify**: `cd packages/core && npx vitest run tests/run-events/stream.spec.ts`.
- **Depends on**: TASK-005

## 6. Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Auth**: N/A for the log file itself. It lives in the run directory under the user's
  `~/.yantra` with default permissions, like the other run artifacts. Socket authentication for
  live readers belongs to FEAT-064. `user_app` exists as a value only; FEAT-068 stamps it, and
  only for authenticated app answers (§7 Consent provenance).
- **Security / privacy**:
  - Every new field is bounded. Text fields come from already-sanitized sources (agent
    summaries, `redactRunInput`) and are control-stripped again.
  - URLs keep origin and path only.
  - No secret, resolved placeholder, page text, environment value or frame is ever recorded.
  - The canary assertions cover the log, an outbound and persisted channel (§7), in TASK-008 and
    TASK-013.
  - `run-events.jsonl` is not added to any model-visible payload.
- **Error Handling**:
  - Typed `RunEventLogError` codes: `RUN_EVENT_LOG_CLOSED`, `RUN_OUTCOME_DUPLICATE`,
    `RUN_EVENT_LOG_OPEN_FAILED`, `RUN_EVENT_INVALID`.
  - A log **open** failure is an environment error before the run proceeds. It goes through the
    run's existing startup-failure path, exits 3, and emits a task failure report, per memory →
    Error Handling.
  - A mid-run **append** failure degrades without aborting the run (§2 Design notes).
  - Subscriber errors are isolated.
  - Nothing is silently swallowed: each case logs once with a stable event name.
- **Logging**: Structured Pino through the injected logger; never event payloads.
  - `run_events_degraded` (`error`, `{code}`);
  - `run_events_after_close` (`warn`, `{kind}`, once per kind);
  - `run_events_listener_failed` (`warn`, `{listener_index, error_class}`, once per listener);
  - `run_events_preopen_overflow` (`warn`, `{dropped}`).
  - The `intervention_*` and `attendance_*` lines in `runtime.jsonl` belong to FEAT-064 and
    FEAT-068, not here.
- **Compatibility**:
  - Every new file is additive, and `events.jsonl` bytes are unchanged (TASK-006 test).
  - Old run directories without `run-events.jsonl` stay fully readable.
  - New enum values are forward-readable only (D7, TASK-002).
- **Performance**:
  - A synchronous small-line append on the hot path.
  - fsync only at the defined points.
  - Readers stream line by line, so a 50,000-event file never loads whole.
